prompt: How do I use the chi squared goodness of fit test to show the correlation between the times of 5k collegiate runners and their altitude
judge_reasoning: The prompt asks specifically how to use the chi-squared goodness-of-fit test to demonstrate a relationship between 5k times and altitude. Response [1] is the closest because it actually invokes a chi-squared goodness-of-fit approach and mentions altitude groups, but it misapplies the GOF framework (expected frequencies/null modeling) and does not truly establish correlation/association between the two variables. Response [4] correctly explains the goodness-of-fit test structure, but it never incorporates altitude or relates results to any time–altitude association. Responses [2] and [3] largely ignore the chi-squared goodness-of-fit requirement and instead propose ANOVA/regression/correlation, making them off-target.
